title: Tensoring K-injectives with bounded split-projective complexes
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site, $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings, and $I^\bullet$ a K-injective cochain complex of sheaves of $R$-modules [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. Let $P^\bullet$ be a bounded cochain complex of sheaves of $R$-modules: $P^r=0$ outside some finite interval of integers. Assume that for every $r$ there are an integer $N_r\geq0$ and maps $i_r:P^r\to R^{N_r}$ and $p_r:R^{N_r}\to P^r$ with $p_ri_r=1$. Then $\operatorname{Tot}(I^\bullet\otimes_R P^\bullet)$, with terms $\bigoplus_{a+r=n}I^a\otimes_R P^r$ and differential $d_I\otimes1+(-1)^a1\otimes d_P$ [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], is K-injective. No boundedness of $I^\bullet$ or vanishing of $d_P$ is assumed.

proof.text: In the additive symmetric monoidal category of sheaves of modules [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], finite powers of the tensor unit are dualizable. For rank zero the product is a zero object. For successor rank, explicitly identify the product with the binary biproduct of the unit and the smaller product, and use closure of dualizable objects under biproducts. The given retractions and the proved source theorem IsDualizable.of_retract then make every term of P dualizable. The additive tensor instances are supplied by the source MonoidalFree module.

source.place: Tag 0FNY, example-dual, duality for finite-free direct summands; implemented using WeilConjectures.CategoryTheory.Monoidal.Dualizable

proof.text: Choose the right dual structure on each term from its proved dualizability. The source construction CochainComplex.rightDual produces a genuine complex D with terms the right duals of P in the opposite degrees, and with its signed transposed differential [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. The bounds a and b on P give bounds -b and -a on D. The proved source theorem exactPairingRightDual supplies evaluation and coevaluation satisfying the triangle identities for P and D. Symmetry reverses this to a dual pair D, P.

source.place: Tag 0FPR, example-dual; Tag 0FNK, more-algebra-lemma-left-dual-complex; implemented using WeilConjectures.Algebra.Homology.Monoidal.Dual

proof.text: Each term of D has P in the opposite degree as a right dual, by swapping the termwise pairing using symmetry. A dualizable object has exact tensor functors (proved source theorem IsDualizable.flat), hence the terms of D are flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Since D is bounded above by -a, [lem-pc-bounded-above-flat-kflat-site] makes D K-flat.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; flatness of dualizable objects from the tensor adjunctions

proof.text: Let Q be the monoidal quotient to the homotopy category. The source theorem ExactPairing.map transports the dual pair D, P through Q, giving the adjunction between right tensoring by Q(D) and right tensoring by Q(P). Given an acyclic A and a map f from A to the tensor complex I tensor P [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves], its class corresponds under this adjunction to a map from Q(A tensor D) to Q(I). K-flatness makes A tensor D acyclic. The characterization IsKInjective.rightOrthogonal of [def-pur-kinjective-complex] makes this adjunct zero. The inverse adjunction bijection sends zero to zero because its tensor functor is a left adjoint and preserves zero morphisms. Injectivity of that bijection makes Q(f) zero, and HomotopyCategory.homotopyOfEq yields a null homotopy of f. This is exactly K-injectivity of I tensor P.
